clue.text: Is he ready to take offence because the waiter served the potato" clumsily?

definitions.text: Is he ready to take offence because the waiter served the potato" clumsily?

parts.words: Is he ready to take offence because the waiter served the potato" clumsily
parts.note: an idiom for someone touchy and quick to feel slighted, pictured literally as a diner with a fried potato slice dropped on him by a clumsy waiter

explanation.surface: A diner bristles after a waiter spills a potato on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The touchy person of the idiom carries a grievance on a part of the body; the clue imagines a real fried potato slice landing there. The phrase fills 1 and 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone with a lingering grievance who is easily provoked into resentment.

clue.text: A theologian's sums

parts.note: a theologian may hold a DD, Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar's arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to total figures, so the verb form matches totals as a plural noun of additions.

clue.text: Fail to make a thorough go of tying the knot?

definitions.text: Fail to make a thorough go of tying the knot?

parts.words: Fail to make a thorough go of tying the knot
parts.note: a half-hearted attempt at a wedding read literally as a knot only half done, a simple sailor's hitch

explanation.surface: Someone only half commits to marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tying the knot' suggests marriage; the answer is a simple knot made by passing a rope's end round a post and through its own loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple knot used by sailors to fasten a rope to a spar or ring.

clue.text: Oil up order in the French Foreign Legion

indicators.note: put in order says the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to grease equipment among French legionnaires.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French slang for a soldier, literally 'hairy one', used especially of First World War infantrymen.
explanation.definitionFit: A French ordinary soldier, the kind found serving in that army.

clue.text: How to exist without having any personal cover?

definitions.text: How to exist without having any personal cover?

parts.words: How to exist without having any personal cover
parts.note: living with no clothing on, or no insurance cover, describes a manner of being unclothed

explanation.surface: Living without insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal cover' sounds like insurance but means clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something without clothes or concealment.

clue.text: Mean time coming with international mire-slinging.

indicators.note: slinging tosses the letters of the muddy word about

explanation.surface: A period of global mud-throwing between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slinging' scrambles MIRE into ERIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Meantime is the period in between, a stopgap interval.

clue.text: Curtseys for shillings

definitions.meaning: small bows or bobbing movements of greeting
old British slang for the shilling coin, worth twelve pence before 1971

explanation.surface: Bows paid for in old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin; its slang name is plural without change.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bend of the knees is a quick dip, and the same word was slang for old twelve-penny coins.

clue.text: … and hatred developing round one trapped in slung mud

parts.note: a round ring shape is the letter O

indicators.note: trapped in says one piece is held inside the other
slung mud is thrown about, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A loathing that grows when someone is stuck in flung mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slung' turns MUD into DUM; 'trapped in' puts I inside to make DIUM, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general loathing or opprobrium directed at someone.

clue.text: Is she learning to become a lady out of her class?

definitions.text: Is she learning to become a lady out of her class?

parts.words: Is she learning to become a lady out of her class
parts.note: social climbing out of one's class read as a pupil studying outside her school form

explanation.surface: A social climber learning manners above her station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' looks like social rank but is a form in school.
explanation.definitionFit: A female pupil learns in class and will one day grow into a woman.

clue.text: A measure in fur that should find a ready market

definitions.text: that should find a ready market

indicators.note: in puts the measure inside the fur

parts.note: sable is a prized fur
an ell is an old cloth measure

explanation.surface: A length of fur that should sell easily.
explanation.walkthrough: An ELL was an old length for cloth, about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are marketable find buyers readily.

clue.text: I held out for a major settlement in India

indicators.note: out says the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to settle a matter in India.
explanation.definitionFit: India's capital territory is one of its largest cities.

clue.text: A little catty but in a coy sort of way

definitions.text: in a coy sort of way

explanation.surface: Slightly spiteful, but bashfully so.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling a young cat, and by extension playfully flirtatious.

clue.text: See 1 across
West Indian dance bending back arm or leg with ring

parts.note: an arm or leg is a limb
a ring is shaped like O

explanation.surface: Dancers lean back with their limbs and a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caribbean dance has performers bend backwards under a lowered bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean dance in which performers lean backwards under a low pole.

clue.text: This direction to join a good company of harpists

definitions.text: This direction to join a good company of harpists

parts.words: This direction to join a good company of harpists
parts.note: angels with harps picture paradise, so the way up to join them is the direction

explanation.surface: A route to a band of harpists.
explanation.walkthrough: Angels are traditionally pictured playing harps in paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means toward the sky or paradise, upward.

clue.text: A seaside outlet for fresh currency

definitions.text: A seaside outlet for fresh currency

parts.words: A seaside outlet for fresh currency
parts.note: a coastal shop for new money read as where a river's freshwater current flows out to sea

explanation.surface: A beach kiosk dealing in new banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currency' looks like money but means the flow of a current; 'fresh' is freshwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A river mouth where fresh water meets the sea tide.

clue.text: By chance it happened to put stress around the centre of bridge

indicators.note: around says the stress word encloses the other piece

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent

indicators.note: the centre of picks the middle letters of the word bridge

explanation.surface: An unplanned emphasis on the middle of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description of the event: something that happened by chance. 'the centre of' and 'around' work on the bridge and stress words.
explanation.definitionFit: An unplanned event is a mishap occurring by chance.

clue.text: Crosby rabble first crowding round curiously

indicators.note: first says the rabble word comes before the singer

parts.note: a rabble is a mob
Bing Crosby, the American crooner

explanation.surface: Crosby's fans swarm around him.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby was a famous American singer and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thronging around someone out of curiosity or hostility.

clue.text: Complex antic rite

indicators.note: complex says the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An elaborate, playful ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' both signals the scrambling and describes the result: the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate, involved ceremony is tangled and detailed.

clue.text: A medium disturbing Clive, eh?

indicators.note: disturbing shakes up the letters of the name and interjection

explanation.surface: A spiritualist rattling Clive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' sounds like a psychic but means a means of conveying something.
explanation.definitionFit: A means of expression or transmission, such as a channel for ideas.

clue.text: Make an armed enclosure for a loved one?

definitions.text: Make an armed enclosure for a loved one?

parts.words: Make an armed enclosure for a loved one
parts.note: a fortified pen read as wrapping one's arms around a dear person

explanation.surface: Building a fortified compound for a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed' suggests weapons but means using arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug is to enclose someone in one's arms.

clue.text: Good man plunged into joy by Dee's 15

indicators.note: plunged into says the saint goes inside the joy word

parts.note: cheer is joy
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A good man plunges into joy by the river Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is ESTUARY; the city sits on the Dee in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An English cathedral city standing where the river Dee widens toward the sea.

clue.text: Lances wound with point, to purify it

indicators.note: wound means twisted round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Cleaning a lance wound with a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past of wind; it turns LANCES into CLEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean thoroughly or make pure.

clue.text: Called a churchman back about a married character

indicators.note: about says the reversed word wraps round the abbreviation
back says the churchman's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a dean is a senior churchman

explanation.surface: A clergyman summoned back over a married figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEAN into NAED; 'about' puts it round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Called means given a title or identified by a label.

clue.text: Stretches a long way back from S.E. Limerick

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something extends far back from south-east Limerick.
explanation.definitionFit: Distances of many land units are long stretches.

clue.text: Forcefully enters new market, perhaps, with treated bearskin

indicators.note: treated, as leather is, says the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A trader cures bearskins to enter a fresh market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' suggests tanning but rearranges BEARSKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To force entry, as a burglar does, or to win a foothold in a market.

clue.text: How Katherine, when 11, may be 22?

parts.note: a pet form of the name Katherine suits a playful young cat, linking 11 and 22

explanation.surface: A girl's name changes with her mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is KITTENISH and 22 is NAMED: a playful Katherine might be called by this pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common diminutive of Katherine that also suggests a young cat.

clue.text: Six-foot workers tunnel through hills

parts.note: tall miners read as six-legged insects digging through their mounds

explanation.surface: Tall labourers dig tunnels through hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-foot' suggests height but means six legs; the hills are their own mounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Six-legged social insects whose worker caste digs tunnels in their mounds.

clue.text: Pitched into an ugly villain without any effect

indicators.note: pitched into, thrown about, says the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Attacking an ugly villain achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ugly' is surface colour; 'Pitched into' rearranges AN and VILLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Done fruitlessly, with no result.

clue.text: Mark that couple

definitions.meaning: Mark the American author of Tom Sawyer, by his pen surname
an old word for two, a pair

explanation.surface: Note that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen surname of Samuel Clemens, and an archaic word for two.

clue.text: Sprinkle powder

definitions.meaning: to scatter fine particles over something

explanation.surface: Scatter talc.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter fine particles, and the fine particles themselves.

clue.text: Lee arranged to make a call about county growers of vegetables

indicators.note: about says the call goes round the reordered name

parts.note: a cry is a call

indicators.note: arranged says the name's letters are reordered

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Lee rings around the county about vegetable growers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London; celery is grown in trenched beds so its stalks can be blanched. 'arranged' and 'about' build the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenches where a stalky crop is raised are plots for producing it.
